questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English-speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I deeply missed my close connections back in Copenhagen and found it challenging to connect with others, partly due to the demanding workload at Boston University.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly straightforward, but there are still many practical details to keep track of when starting at a new university in the U.S. at the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The study abroad coordinator provided guidance by sending emails outlining the necessary tasks and hosting a pre-lecture at the start of the semester with practical information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We got the necessary information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed in an Airbnb apartment with another student from my home university, which was in a very nice area. However, living in Boston is quite expensive, and I faced significant issues with my landlord, who tried to demand additional money from me after I moved out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's very expensive. Be sure to take photos and videos of the entire apartment when you move in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Both off-campus and on-campus are extremely expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did it before arriving, and it was pretty accessible.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You simply need to register for the courses you want on a website. You can make changes to your selection until about a week after the courses begin.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You had about a week to switch to another course, during which you could ask the professors about the course and what to expect.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It wasn't very successful. When I was choosing Boston University, many courses appeared available, but that was because you can't distinguish between fall and spring courses initially. As a result, many of the courses I wanted—and that were a major reason I chose Boston University—weren't available when I registered. So, be aware of that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the courses available to you may not be clear when you choose Boston University.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The workload was very heavy, but the professors were excellent and highly engaged.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two BA courses and one MA course. The MA course was at a high level, but overall, I wouldn't necessarily say the course level is higher than at Copenhagen University, even though the workload is significantly greater.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar to Copenhagen, with lectures in large auditoriums and discussions in smaller classes. However, one of my courses had a very small class of only 15 students, so we all met every time. Compared to Copenhagen University, the discussion sessions were shorter and, from my perspective, not as useful as they often are in Copenhagen. On the other hand, the lectures were often very useful and interesting.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Principles of Neuroscience, System Biology and Introduction to Computer Science.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of my courses; they were all very informative and interesting. Systems Biology was the MA class, which included several PhD students, so I was a bit intimidated at first, but it worked out well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The mandatory insurance for all students at Boston University is very expensive, which I didn't expect.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The mobile subscription is much more expensive compared to Denmark. Overall, everything is quite costly, including grocery stores.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I played some soccer there, but the skill level was either very high or very low.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Overall, there are many club opportunities, including an event with all of the clubs presenting themselves at the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club that interests you, as there are many different options to choose from.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go whale watching, visit the many cozy cafes and restaurants, and take a walk through the city. Also, be sure to watch sports, both on and off-campus! It's fun—I saw basketball, American football, baseball, and ice hockey more than once.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to connect with the American students already living in Boston. Additionally, they tend to be very young when starting university in the U.S., which is noticeable when you're on campus.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go into clubs!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I mostly found it challenging to be in a new city, far from home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People in Boston are very friendly. For instance, I noticed that everyone always holds the door open for you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I found it challenging on many levels—feeling alone in a new city far from home, and also adjusting to studying at a new university where things are done differently. If you want to have a group to connect with and spend most of your time with, I recommend living on campus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to take pictures when you arrive at your apartment or room!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: When having success in the most challenging presentations, projects and exams.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my family, friends, and boyfriend, and feeling lonely.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
